transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um, I guess what brings me in is... well, my eating has gotten a little off lately. It's probably nothing major, but some days I barely get down, like, a coffee and a granola bar before a shift. And I've noticed my work scrubs have been hanging pretty loose on me, even though I'm really not trying to lose weight at all. 

I just wanted to get it checked out... is that an okay reason to come see you? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to.
Are you trying to restrict your food intake?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I'm really not trying to restrict what I eat at all. I know how important it is to keep my strength up, especially working at the hospital. I wouldn't do anything like that on purpose, I promise. 

It's just... I don't know, I just haven't had the appetite for it. Like I was saying, I'll just have that coffee and maybe a granola bar, and that's really all I can manage before a shift. And then I noticed my scrubs getting so baggy... but it's really not intentional, doctor. I hope you don't think I'm doing this to myself on purpose. Does that make sense?
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?

Oh, no, definitely not. I... I don't really do that at all. Honestly, it's kind of the exact opposite right now. I just can't seem to stomach much of anything at one time. 

I would absolutely tell you if I did, I promise. I just don't have the urge to sit down and eat a whole bunch of food like that. Um, is that... I mean, is it helpful that I'm explaining it this way? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way so you can do your job.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight recently?

Well, um, I guess I have lost some weight, yeah. Like I mentioned before, my work scrubs have just been hanging really loose on me lately. I haven't stepped on a scale or anything, so I don't know the exact number, but... it's definitely enough that I've noticed it in how my clothes fit. 

But I really want to be clear, it's not because I'm trying to. It's just that my eating has been so off, and some days I really do just barely get down that coffee and a granola bar before I go in for a shift. I hope that's not too bad... I mean, I'm trying my best to keep up with things. Is it okay that I don't know the exact amount of weight I've lost? I can try to weigh myself when I get home if you need me to.
Have you been feeling anxious or depressed lately?

Well, um... I guess I have been feeling a little down. I really try not to let it get to me, because I know I need to be positive at the hospital, and I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining to you. But... yeah, if I'm being completely honest. 

Most mornings, I wake up with this... this heavy, hollow feeling. It almost feels like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge. I try my absolute best to push through it, I really do. I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or like I'm not trying hard enough to keep my spirits up. Is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you think your eating has been affected by your feeling down?

Um... I mean, maybe? I don't really want to blame it on that, because I feel like I should just be able to eat normally, you know? Like, it's just food. But... I guess when I'm feeling really empty in the mornings, the idea of eating just doesn't sound good at all. 

I really try to force something down, though. I don't want you to think I'm just giving up or letting it get the best of me. I know nutrition is important, especially working in healthcare. I just... I guess they could be connected. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overcomplicating it. I just want to be helpful.
Is it that you're just not interested in eating when you wake up feeling down, or is it more that the thought of food is unappealing to you?

Um, well... I guess it's more that I'm just not interested? Like I was mentioning earlier about how my eating has gotten so off, where I barely get down that coffee and granola bar before my shift... it's not that food grosses me out or anything. I really don't want you to think I'm doing this on purpose or that I'm refusing to eat. 

It's just... when I wake up feeling that down, eating just doesn't even cross my mind. It feels like a chore I just don't have the energy for. And I guess that's exactly why my scrubs have been hanging so loose lately, even though I'm really, truly not trying to lose weight at all. I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right. Did that answer your question okay?
Do you think there's anything physically wrong with you that might be causing you to not feel like eating?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really hope not. I haven't noticed any physical pain or, you know, stomach issues or anything like that. I really try to take good care of my health, being around patients all day, so I'd like to think physically I'm doing okay. 

I guess I just... I don't want to make excuses, you know? It's probably just my mood getting in the way of my appetite, like we were talking about. I really don't think it's a medical problem with my body. Does that sound right to you? I'd hate to be missing something important, but I really feel like physically, I'm fine. I hope that's the right answer.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um, I really don't want you to think I'm, like, obsessing over my weight or trying to be overly thin or anything like that. I actually feel a little bad that I've lost some weight recently, to be honest. 

I know how important it is to stay healthy and keep my strength up, especially for my job. I'm not afraid of gaining weight at all. In fact, I'd probably feel a lot better if I could just get back to my normal size and fill out my scrubs again. I really hope I'm not coming across as someone who is intentionally restricting food. I just want to be healthy, you know? Does that make sense?
Do you think your loss of appetite started around the same time as your feelings of depression?

Um, yes, I... I think they definitely started around the same time. I really hope I'm explaining this clearly, but yeah, it's like they're tied together. 

It's just... most mornings, I wake up with this heavy, almost hollow feeling. Like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge for work. And when I feel that low, the thought of eating just doesn't even register. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being dramatic about the mornings, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline. 

So, yes, the mood and the not eating definitely seemed to hit at the same time. I hope that helps answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you think you would have a normal appetite if you weren't feeling depressed?

Um, yeah, I... I really think I would. I mean, I used to have a pretty good appetite. But lately, it's just gotten so off. Some days I barely get down, like, a coffee and a granola bar before a whole shift. 

And, um, I don't want you to think I'm doing this on purpose, but my scrubs have actually been hanging loose on me. I'm really not trying to lose weight, I promise. It's just... I guess the depression just takes away the urge to eat. I really hope I'm making sense. Do you think that's normal for someone feeling this way? I just want to make sure I'm not doing something wrong.
Do you think your appetite would return to normal if your depression improved?

Um, yes, absolutely. I really believe it would. I mean, like I was saying before, the main reason I even realized I needed help and came in was because my eating has gotten so far off track. 

I'm really hoping that if we can fix the depression, I won't just be living off that coffee and granola bar anymore. I just want to get back to eating normally so my scrubs fit right again and stop hanging off me. I really don't want to be this thin, I promise. I just want to be a good, healthy employee again. Do you think treating the depression will help fix all of that? I really hope I'm on the right track with this.
Did the depression start before or after you first noticed changes in your eating habits?

Um, the depression actually came a bit later. I really hope I'm not confusing things after what I just said, but... well, the changes in my eating kind of started first, and then the steady depression and just... losing interest in everything else settled in after that. 

It's been with me for roughly the past year and four months now. I really hope I'm not being too much of a bother by correcting the timeline a little bit. I just want to make sure you have the exact right information so you can help me. Does that timeline make sense to you? I really want to be helpful and get this right.
Do you think something specific triggered your depression, or did it just start on its own?

Um, well, I... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I genuinely like my clinic and I always try to be a good team player. But, um, I think there was a specific trigger. 

This has all been going on since the clinic's EMR and workflow overhaul changed my hours, which was almost two years ago now. I really tried my best to just adjust and not make a fuss about it, I promise. I wanted to be helpful during the transition. But I think that's when things really started shifting for me. 

I hope it doesn't make me sound weak that a schedule change and some new computer software threw me off so much. Do you think it's normal for a work change like that to trigger all of this? I just want to make sure I'm not overreacting or making excuses.
Do you think your lack of appetite would still be a problem if your depression were successfully treated?

Um, I mean, I really hope it wouldn't be a problem anymore. I know I mentioned this a little bit already, but honestly, the eating thing is the main reason I'm here. It's just gotten so off track. 

I really don't want you to think I'm doing this on purpose or anything, but some days I barely manage to get down a coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift starts. And I know it's bad because my scrubs are just hanging off me now, and they used to fit perfectly fine. I promise I'm not trying to lose weight or anything like that. I just... I want to be healthy again. 

If the depression gets better, I really, really want to believe my eating will go back to normal too. Do you think that's how it usually works? I just want to make sure I'm focusing on the right things so I can get back to doing a good job at work.
Do you think your eating would improve if your mood improved?

Um, yeah, I... I really think it would. I mean, I hope it would. Like I said, I'm really not trying to be difficult about eating, it's just... when I feel so down, the thought of food just doesn't even register. 

If my mood was better, I think I'd actually want to eat again. I'd definitely try my best to, anyway. I really want to get back to normal and stop worrying you and everyone else about my weight. Do you think treating the depression is the right first step for that? I really trust your judgment on this.
Do you find that your appetite changes significantly when you're having a particularly bad day emotionally?

Um, yes, I really do. I know I keep bringing this up, and I'm so sorry if I sound like a broken record, but... yeah, on the really bad days emotionally, that's exactly when my eating gets the most off track. 

Like I was saying before, those are the mornings where I can barely force down a coffee and a granola bar before my shift starts. I really don't mean to do it, my stomach just sort of completely shuts down when my mood drops. And I think because I've had quite a few of those bad days lately, that's why my scrubs are hanging so loose on me now. I promise I'm really not trying to lose weight or be difficult. 

Honestly, the weight loss and the eating is really what brought me in to see you, because I just want to be healthy and look presentable for work again. I don't want my supervisors to think I'm not taking care of myself. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I keep focusing on the eating part, I just want to give you all the right information.
Do you find that your appetite returns to normal on days when you're feeling emotionally better?

Um, well... I guess I haven't really had many days lately where I feel completely better emotionally, so it's a little hard to say for sure. But I want to say yes? I really hope it would. 

I know I've mentioned this a lot, and I hope I'm not overstepping by repeating myself, but the eating thing really is the main reason I came in to see you. It's just... some days I'm only managing that coffee and a granola bar before my shift, and my scrubs are just hanging so loose now. I really, really want to stress that I'm not doing this on purpose or trying to lose weight. I just want to get back on track and be a good employee. 

If I can just get to a place where I'm having more good days emotionally, I really believe my appetite will come back. I'll definitely do my best to make sure it does, anyway. Does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
Is your loss of appetite the main issue you're struggling with right now?

Um, yes, I think so. I mean, I know I've brought it up a few times already, and I really hope I'm not being annoying by focusing on it so much. But yes, the eating thing is really what pushed me to make the appointment. 

It's just that it's gotten so off track lately. Like I mentioned, some days I'm barely getting down that coffee and a granola bar before my shift starts. And I really don't want to look unprofessional at work, but my scrubs have been hanging so loose on me. I just want to reassure you again that I'm really not trying to lose weight or anything like that. I just want to get this sorted out so I can do my job properly and not worry anyone. Is it okay that I'm so focused on the eating part? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information to help me fix this.
